author: Asmae
title: Object-Oriented Programming (Python)
extends: COMP101_ONTOLOGY.json (static curriculum ontology) — no longer treated as an active cross-reference target for this module; this file is self-contained and validated on its own terms (see validate.py / configs/comp101_oop.json).

entity_types.name: Lecture
entity_types.definition: A course unit defined by the curriculum with a sequence number, title, and learning outcomes. Organizational — groups content and defines ordering, doesn't itself teach anything.

entity_types.name: Concept
entity_types.definition: A pure abstract idea or theoretical principle with no runtime existence, syntax, or physical form (e.g. Inheritance, Encapsulation, Polymorphism).

entity_types.name: DataType
entity_types.definition: A Python-level classification of values determining valid operations and storage — what type() would return.

entity_types.name: Skill
entity_types.definition: A transferable cognitive operation a student can perform across multiple unseen problems, defined by a verb phrase (e.g. "Apply polymorphism").

entity_types.name: Method
entity_types.definition: A callable defined on a specific Python type, accessed via dot notation (e.g. __str__, __init__).

entity_types.name: BuiltInFunction
entity_types.definition: A Python callable pre-defined in the built-in/stdlib namespace, invoked as a free function (e.g. isinstance(), super(), hasattr()).

entity_types.name: LanguageConstruct
entity_types.definition: A syntactic keyword, statement, or structural element of Python grammar itself (e.g. class, def, return).

entity_types.name: ErrorType
entity_types.definition: A named Python exception class that can be raised when an operation fails (e.g. AttributeError, TypeError, ValueError, NotImplementedError, RuntimeError).

entity_types.name: OOPMechanism
entity_types.definition: A concrete Python-level procedure/convention that makes OOP work at the implementation level — the how, as opposed to Concept's what (e.g. Constructor, Self Reference, Name Mangling, super() Call, Dunder Method).

entity_types.name: ClassMember
entity_types.definition: A named structural element belonging to a class definition or hierarchy — a structural slot, not a behavior (e.g. Instance Attribute, Class Attribute, Subclass, Superclass).

entity_types.name: MethodRole
entity_types.definition: The contract a method fulfills within a class, independent of its concrete implementation (e.g. Getter Method, Abstract Method, Static Method).

entity_types.name: DesignAbstraction
entity_types.definition: Language-agnostic structural/architectural design vocabulary above the level of any individual class or method (e.g. Abstract Class, Interface, Mixin, Design Pattern).

entity_types.name: PythonInternals
entity_types.definition: A CPython interpreter-level mechanism exposing how classes/objects are built and accessed (e.g. Decorator, Metaclass, __slots__, __mro__).

entity_types.name: Algorithm
entity_types.definition: A specific algorithmic solution/procedure for a well-defined problem. Declared as of v2.4 solely so it can participate in the TypeProducer domain union (see relations -> producesType/acceptsType) and in the AllDisjointClasses axiom. Deliberately has zero individuals in this module — OOP doesn't introduce new algorithms — this is schema-level completeness, not a content gap.

relations.name: taughtIn
relations.definition: Content belongs to / is first introduced in a lecture.

relations.name: dependsOn
relations.definition: Subject cannot be meaningfully learned until the object is already understood. Prerequisite ordering between concepts/skills.

relations.name: contrastsWith
relations.definition: Subject and object are alternatives/opposites or commonly confused peers at the same level of abstraction.

relations.name: usesConcept
relations.definition: A non-Concept entity actively applies/draws on a Concept to do its work.

relations.name: producesType
relations.definition: A Method/BuiltInFunction/Algorithm actually yields a result of the given DataType. Domain widened from Method-only to the TypeProducer union in v2.4.

relations.name: acceptsType
relations.definition: Performing the subject operation requires/accepts an argument of the given DataType. Added in v2.4, mirrors producesType's domain (TypeProducer) but for input rather than output. Only asserted where a BuiltInFunction/Method has one universally-fixed parameter type across every call (e.g. hasattr()'s name is always str) — not asserted for user-defined-signature methods like __init__/__eq__, whose parameter types vary per class.

relations.name: throwsError
relations.definition: Performing the subject operation can actually raise the named ErrorType under realistic conditions covered by this course. Beginner-friendliness is a deliberate filter: e.g. super()'s real RuntimeError and hasattr()'s edge-case TypeError were considered and only added where the course actually expects students to hit them.

relations.name: exampleOf
relations.definition: The subject is a specific, concrete instance/exemplar of the general object concept or mechanism (e.g. __init__ exampleOf Constructor, Mixin exampleOf Design Pattern). Used since v2.2 in place of partOf for concrete-realization pairs that aren't true compositional containment.

relations.name: implementedBy
relations.definition: A Concept is made concrete in Python code by a LanguageConstruct/Method/OOPMechanism/PythonInternals.

relations.name: bestPractice
relations.definition: A recommended approach or convention associated with this entity. Datatype property, not a node.

relations.name: enables
relations.definition: Subject is a mechanism/language feature that makes the object concept/goal achievable — means-to-end, not prerequisite (contrast with dependsOn).

relations.name: partOf
relations.definition: Subject is a genuine conceptual/structural sub-component of the object. Used here for Method/MethodRole -> containing Concept membership, in place of the official schema's narrower method_of.

official_relations_not_used_here: PREREQUISITE_OF (no cross-lecture ordering — this module has only L10)
OPERATES_ON_TYPE (no Operator individuals in this module)
TIME_COMPLEXITY (no Algorithm individuals in this module — the class is declared but deliberately empty, see entity_types)
SOLVES_PROBLEM (no Algorithm individuals in this module)
graph_traversal: As of v2.5, every relation in this module is bidirectionally materialized as real triples, not left to reasoner inference: all 10 inverse-property pairs (dependsOn/isRequiredBy, usesConcept/isUsedBy, throwsError/isThrownBy, producesType/isProducedBy, implementedBy/implements, enables/enabledBy, partOf/hasPart, exampleOf/hasExample, taughtIn/teaches, acceptsType/isAcceptedBy) have both directions asserted, and all 11 contrastsWith pairs have both directions asserted too (22 raw triples covering 11 unique relationships — dedupe by unordered pair if rendering, e.g. the HTML poster generator does this to avoid drawing doubled arrows). A raw SPARQL/triple-pattern query can now walk any edge from either endpoint without running a reasoner first.
notes: ImplementorType (owl:equivalentClass of a unionOf LanguageConstruct/Method/OOPMechanism/PythonInternals) and TypeProducer (owl:equivalentClass of a unionOf Method/BuiltInFunction/Algorithm, added v2.4) are both helper union classes used only as property domain/range — neither is an instantiated entity type, no individuals are typed directly as either. Watch out: their equivalentClass-to-anonymous-blank-node encoding means naive 'count all owl:Class subjects' tooling (e.g. the OntoQA class_richness metric) will see 2 extra phantom classes beyond the 14 real entity types listed above; this is a metric-counting quirk, not a modeling error. Datatype annotation properties definition, courseId, cognitiveType and commonCauses are present on most individuals but aren't modeled as relations here since they're plumbing (labels/IDs), not the semantic relations. Encoding (an entity type in earlier versions) was removed in v2.2: it had zero individuals in this module and was ICS-ontology territory, not OOP. This module no longer tracks or documents overlap with the static curriculum ontology (COMP101_ONTOLOGY.json) as an open concern — that comparison is out of scope; this file and comp101_L10.owl are treated as self-contained and validated independently (see validate.py --config configs/comp101_oop.json, which passes structural/HermiT/OOPS/OntoQA/SPARQL-CQ/skill-graph checks as of v2.5).
